newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ACCESS energy prices extend daytime losses.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ACCESS energy prices extend daytime losses.

text.p: U.S. energy futures, which fell during the day, continued down in the after-hours market, as traders sold off contracts on concerns crude prices would keep weakening, brokers said.
Crude oil for May delivery failed to breach $19.79 a barrel during Wednesday trade, a "technical" signal that it was unable to rise in the near-term, according to analysts who chart price trends.
Crude oil for May delivery ended eight cents lower on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) Wednesday, settling at $19.27 a barrel.

After U.S. government reports showed lower stocks of petroleum products, crude prices rose early Wednesday. But with nationwide crude supply up 1.05 million barrels, the market soon cooled, according to traders.
On ACCESS, the NYMEX after-hours market, May crude fell 16 cents a barrel to trade $19.11. About 1,038 lots traded overall and 484 in the front month.
Unleaded gasoline for May delivery was traded 60.30 cents gallon, off 0.40 cents from the settle as 31 lots traded in the front month and 55 overall, traders said.
NYMEX May heating oil rose 0.11 cents from the market close of 53.11, with total volume at 235 lots, and 387 lots traded in May, traders said.
